titleText.en: For years, I took the wrong lesson from that Monster Cable experiment and only listened to my music through alligator-clipped coat hangers.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish archive supplies an empty title-text attribute, preserved exactly in the Spanish field; the English field preserves the complete official title text. The Spanish raster localizes the dialogue and sale signs, preserves technical labels as audited exclusions, joins the visible AL-/TAVOCES, ALTA-/VOCES, SABO-/REAR, and SIS-/TEMA line wraps as single words, and prints CLIC as a lexical sound effect.

regions.labelEs: ¿TENEMOS UN CABLE RCA A 3,5MM HEMBRA-HEMBRA? VOY A COMPRAR UNOS ALTAVOCES PARA LA NUEVA XBOX, YA QUE EL MONITOR NO TIENE.

excludedUnits.rationale: RCA is a connector initialism rather than Spanish lexical vocabulary.
This printed connector size is a numerical measurement rather than a Spanish word.
XBOX is the printed product name rather than Spanish lexical vocabulary.

applications.exampleEs: TENEMOS UN CABLE RCA A 3,5MM HEMBRA-HEMBRA
applications.explanationEn: The opening question marks and intonation turn this otherwise statement-shaped request into a yes-or-no question.
Voy matches the speaker, a supplies the link, and comprar stays in its unchanged dictionary form.
Nueva appears before the product name and highlights that it is the newly released or newly relevant model.
Nueva uses its feminine singular ending to match the understood feminine treatment of the product name.
Ya and que form the causal connector that introduces the following reason.
The opening question marks and intonation turn this otherwise statement-shaped clause into a yes-or-no question.
Cutres follows the noun altavoces in the usual neutral descriptive order.
The plural ending on cutres matches the plural noun altavoces; this adjective uses the same form for masculine and feminine.

regions.labelEs: ¿QUÉ IMPORTA? SOLO QUIERO OÍR SI ME DISPARAN, NO SABOREAR TODO EL DETALLE DE UN BELLO PAISAJE SONORO MUSICAL.

applications.explanationEn: Qué directly asks what importance the issue has, so it carries a written accent.
Quiero changes for the speaker, while oír keeps its unchanged dictionary form.
Bello comes before paisaje to foreground the speaker's positive evaluation.
The two descriptive words follow paisaje in neutral descriptive order.
Bello and sonoro use masculine singular forms to match paisaje; musical has one singular form for either gender.
Paisaje and sonoro combine as the established term for a sound environment.

regions.labelEs: TÚ JAMÁS HAS ESCUCHADO UN BELLO PAISAJE MUSICAL. TÚ ESCUCHAS RIPEOS EN FLV DE YOUTUBE A 96 KBPS.

excludedUnits.rationale: FLV is a technical file-format initialism rather than Spanish vocabulary.
YOUTUBE is the printed service name rather than Spanish vocabulary.
This printed bitrate value is a number rather than Spanish vocabulary.
KBPS is a technical bitrate-unit initialism rather than Spanish vocabulary.

applications.explanationEn: Has matches one familiar listener, and escuchado supplies the completed listening action.
Bello precedes paisaje to foreground a positive evaluation.
Musical follows paisaje in neutral descriptive order.
Bello is masculine singular to match paisaje, while musical uses the same singular form for either gender.

regions.labelEs: SÍ, LO QUE TÚ DIGAS, PERO VOY A COMPRAR ESTOS ALTAVOCES DE 20$. CON 5 VATIOS HABRÁ DE SOBRA.

excludedUnits.rationale: This printed price is a numerical monetary amount rather than Spanish vocabulary.
This printed power quantity is a number rather than Spanish vocabulary.

applications.explanationEn: Lo que introduces the open-ended content, tú emphasizes the listener, and digas supplies the conceding form.
Voy matches the speaker, a links the verbs, and comprar remains in its dictionary form.
Habrá is the irregular future form used for what will exist; its ending still marks future time.
De and sobra form the fixed expression describing an ample surplus.

regions.labelEs: ¿5 VATIOS PARA UN SISTEMA DE SONIDO DE SALÓN? ¿ES UNA BROMA?

excludedUnits.rationale: This printed power quantity is a number rather than Spanish vocabulary.

applications.explanationEn: Sistema names the equipment set, and de sonido states its audio function.
Question marks and intonation turn the statement-shaped words into a yes-or-no question.

regions.labelEs: NO, ESTO ES UNA BROMA: ¿CUÁNTOS AUDIÓFILOS HACEN FALTA PARA CAMBIAR UNA BOMBILLA?

applications.explanationEn: Cuántos directly asks for a masculine plural number and therefore keeps its written accent.
Hacen is plural because the people being counted are plural, while falta stays unchanged.
Para introduces the purpose, and cambiar remains in its dictionary form.
Cuántos stands alone as a direct question asking for a masculine plural number.

regions.labelEs: LUEGO TE LO DIGO, NO PODRÍAS APRECIAR EL REMATE DEL CHISTE A TRAVÉS DE ESTE CÓDEC TELEFÓNICO DE 12KBPS.

excludedUnits.rationale: This printed bitrate is a numerical technical measurement rather than Spanish vocabulary.

applications.explanationEn: Podrías keeps the irregular poder stem and adds the informal-singular conditional ending -ías.
Podrías supplies the imagined ability, while apreciar remains in its dictionary form.
The three fixed words introduce the medium through which the sound would pass.
Telefónico follows the noun códec in neutral descriptive order.
Telefónico uses the masculine singular ending to match códec.

cards.questionEn: How can Spanish turn an ordinary statement into a yes-or-no question?
cards.answerEn: Use question marks and questioning intonation; Spanish does not need a separate helper like English do or does.
cards.noteEn: The word order can remain the same as in a statement, especially in conversation. The opening and closing question marks show the question in writing.
Cable can name an electrical or signal-carrying wire, not only a television service.

cards.answerEn: to (links one connector type to another)
cards.noteEn: In descriptions of adapters and cables, a links the connector at one end to the connector at the other end.

example.es: Compré un adaptador de USB a HDMI.

cards.noteEn: For connectors, hembra describes a socket that receives a plug. A repeated pair such as hembra-hembra says both ends are sockets.

cards.answerEn: Use a form of ir (“to go”), then a, then the action verb in its dictionary form.
cards.noteEn: Ir changes to match the person: voy a means “I am going to,” vas a means “you are going to,” and va a means “he/she is going to.” The final action stays in its unchanged -ar, -er, or -ir form. This pattern expresses a plan, intention, or expected future event.
cards.questionEn: How do you say that someone is going to do something?

cards.answerEn: to (part of ir a + infinitive, going to do something)
some; a few (before a masculine plural noun)
cards.noteEn: Unos introduces an indefinite masculine plural group or amount. Use unas before a feminine plural noun.
Altavoces is the plural of altavoz, a device that produces sound.

example.es: Los altavoces están junto al televisor.
example.en: The speakers are next to the television.

cards.noteEn: Para can introduce the person, animal, or thing that something is meant for. This differs from para before an action verb, where it expresses a purpose such as “in order to.”

cards.promptEs: una nueva persona o cosa · una persona o cosa nueva
cards.questionEn: What difference can the position of nuevo make?
cards.answerEn: Before the person or thing, nuevo often means newly added or newly in that role; after it, nuevo more often stresses that the thing itself is brand-new.
cards.noteEn: Nuevo changes to nueva, nuevos, or nuevas to match what it describes. Una nueva compañera usually means someone who has recently become a coworker or classmate. Una mesa nueva more often means a newly made or unused table. Context can blur the contrast, so this is a common tendency rather than an absolute rule.

cards.promptEs: adjetivo que concuerda con masculino o femenino
cards.questionEn: How does a Spanish describing word change for a man, woman, or gendered noun?
cards.answerEn: Make the describing word match the gender and number of the person or thing it describes.
cards.noteEn: Many describing words ending in -o change to -a for a feminine singular person or noun: cansado becomes cansada. Plurals normally add -s. Some describing words have one form for both genders.

example.es: Pedro está cansado y Ana está cansada.
example.en: Pedro is tired and Ana is tired.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; begins ya que, because or since
cards.noteEn: Ya and que form a causal connector. This fixed ya does not mean “already.”

example.es: Me fui, ya que era tarde.
example.en: I left because it was late.

cards.questionEn: How do you introduce a reason with a phrase meaning “because” or “since”?
cards.answerEn: Use ya que before the reason.
cards.noteEn: Ya que is a fixed two-word connector. It introduces an explanation treated as known or relevant; the verb after it uses the ordinary statement form when the reason is presented as a fact.

example.es: Tomamos el autobús, ya que llovía.
example.en: We took the bus because it was raining.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; completes ya que, because or since
cards.noteEn: Que completes the fixed causal connector ya que and introduces the reason that follows.

example.es: Cerramos, ya que no había clientes.
example.en: We closed because there were no customers.

cards.noteEn: Monitor is masculine: el monitor.

cards.questionEn: Where does a basic Spanish describing word usually go relative to its noun?
cards.answerEn: Put it after the noun in the common neutral order.
cards.noteEn: Many ordinary descriptive words follow the person or thing they describe: un coche rojo, una casa grande. Some adjectives commonly come before the noun, and moving an adjective can change emphasis or meaning, so this is a useful default rather than an absolute rule.
Cutre is informal and dismissive. It describes something as shabby, low-quality, or embarrassingly cheap.

cards.answerEn: often no separate English word; links a noun to another noun that names its type or use
cards.noteEn: Spanish often uses de between two nouns where English uses a noun directly before another noun. For example, una taza de café is ‘a coffee cup,’ and material de oficina is ‘office material.’
As a noun in computing, el portátil is a laptop. As an adjective, portátil means portable.

example.es: Mi portátil necesita una batería nueva.
example.en: My laptop needs a new battery.

cards.answerEn: oh; an exclamation of alarm or annoyance
Write qué, cómo, cuándo, and similar words with an accent when they ask a question or add an exclamation.
cards.noteEn: This includes direct questions (¿Qué quieres?), questions inside another sentence (No sé qué quiere), and exclamations (¡Qué bonito!). Without the accent, these words usually connect parts of a sentence instead: el libro que quiero means “the book that I want.”
cards.questionEn: Why do words such as que, como, and cuando sometimes have a written accent?
How do you say what someone wants to do?
cards.answerEn: Use a form of querer, then the action verb in its unchanged dictionary form.
cards.noteEn: The dictionary form is the unchanged verb ending in -ar, -er, or -ir. Querer changes to match the person and time, while the desired action stays unchanged: quiero salir, quieres comer, queremos dormir. Spanish does not insert a between the two verbs.
Oír means to perceive a sound. Its written accent keeps the two vowel sounds in separate syllables.

cards.answerEn: whether; if (introducing an indirect yes-or-no question)
cards.noteEn: Unaccented si can introduce a condition or an indirect yes-or-no question. In me pregunto si, English usually uses “whether.” Accented sí means “yes.”

example.en: I do not know whether it is open.

cards.answerEn: they shoot at; they fire at
cards.noteEn: Disparan is a present form of disparar for they or you plural. A short object word can identify the target.

example.en: The guards fire into the air.

cards.noteEn: Saborear literally means to savor a flavor. It can also mean taking time to enjoy or appreciate an experience in detail.

example.en: I want to savor every moment.

cards.noteEn: Before el plus a masculine singular noun, todo means the whole amount or extent of it: todo el día, todo el trabajo.
Detalle names one small, specific part of a larger whole.
Bello is an evaluative adjective. It changes to bella for a feminine singular noun and to bellos or bellas in the plural.

cards.questionEn: Where do common judgment words such as bueno or malo often go?
cards.answerEn: Put them before the noun when they give an overall evaluation: buena idea, mala noticia.
cards.noteEn: Spanish often puts a neutral descriptive word after its noun, but common evaluation words can come before it. The describing word still changes to match the noun: bueno becomes buena before a feminine singular noun.
Paisaje can describe the visible scenery of a place and also appears figuratively in compounds such as paisaje sonoro.

example.es: El paisaje cambia junto al mar.
example.en: The landscape changes by the sea.

cards.questionEn: How do you refer to the complete collection of sounds in a place or experience?
cards.noteEn: Paisaje literally means landscape, and sonoro relates to sound. Together they form the established term “soundscape,” covering the sounds that characterize an environment or recording.

example.es: Grabaron el paisaje sonoro del bosque.

cards.noteEn: Sonoro describes something made of, relating to, or rich in sound.

example.es: El museo creó un mapa sonoro.
example.en: The museum created a sound map.

cards.noteEn: Musical has the same singular form with masculine and feminine nouns; add -es for the plural.
Jamás is a strong way to say “never.” Like nunca, it can appear after a verb already negated with no, or before the verb without no.

cards.answerEn: Use he, has, ha, hemos, habéis, or han followed by the verb’s completed-action form.
cards.noteEn: These are forms of haber, the helper verb used here like English “have.” For most verbs, the completed-action form ends in -ado after an -ar verb and -ido after an -er or -ir verb. This form is called the past participle, and it does not change after haber. How often this tense is used instead of the simple past varies by region.
cards.questionEn: How do you say “have done,” as in “I have finished”?

cards.noteEn: Escuchado is the completed-action form of escuchar. It follows a form of haber: he escuchado, has escuchado, and so on.

example.en: I have never heard that song.

cards.noteEn: Escuchar goes directly before what is heard. Spanish does not add a separate word for the English “to” in “listen to.”

example.en: I listen to music at home.

cards.noteEn: Ripeo is computing slang for a digital copy extracted from another recording or medium. Ripeos is plural.

example.es: Guardó varios ripeos de sus discos.
example.en: He saved several rips of his discs.

cards.questionEn: Why does the final comment undermine the criticism of the speakers?
cards.answerEn: The supposed audio expert demands high fidelity while relying on heavily compressed sources and an even lower-quality phone connection.
cards.noteEn: Audiophiles value accurate sound reproduction. The speaker mocks cheap equipment, yet listens to low-bitrate video rips; the call's still lower bitrate then becomes the excuse for withholding the punchline. The mismatch between claimed standards and actual listening conditions drives the joke.

example.es: Un audiófilo comparó dos grabaciones con distinta compresión.
example.en: An audiophile compared two recordings with different compression.

cards.answerEn: at (introducing a measured distance, speed, or rate)

cards.noteEn: At the start of a statement, sí can acknowledge that a point is true before adding a contrast, often with pero. English may use “yes,” “admittedly,” or “granted” for this use.

example.es: Sí, es caro, pero dura muchos años.
example.en: Granted, it is expensive, but it lasts many years.

cards.answerEn: what; that which (as part of lo que)
cards.noteEn: Lo combines with que to refer to an idea, action, or whole situation rather than a masculine noun. Together, lo que means “what” or “the thing that.”

cards.questionEn: How can you concede or dismissively accept whatever another person says?
cards.noteEn: Lo que refers to “whatever” is said, tú names one familiar listener for emphasis, and digas is the special form used in this open-ended concession. Tone can make the response sincere or dismissive.

example.es: De acuerdo, lo que tú digas.

cards.answerEn: what; that which (as part of lo que)
cards.noteEn: Here que completes lo que, a neutral expression meaning “what” or “the thing that.” It does not refer to a particular masculine or feminine noun.

cards.answerEn: you say (in a dismissive or conceding response)
cards.noteEn: Digas is a special form of decir for one familiar listener. Fixed responses such as lo que tú digas use it to concede or dismiss whatever the other person says.
De plus a noun phrase can describe what kind of thing something is or a characteristic it has. English may use “with,” “having,” or a compound adjective.

example.es: Buscan una casa de gran tamaño.
example.en: They are looking for a large house.

cards.noteEn: Vatio is the Spanish unit name for a watt, a measure of power. Vatios is plural.
Habrá is the future existence form of haber. It uses the irregular future stem habr- plus -á and stays singular even when what will exist is plural.

example.en: There will be more options tomorrow.

cards.questionEn: How do you say what someone will do in Spanish?
cards.answerEn: Keep the action verb in its dictionary form and add a future ending such as -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -éis, or -án.
cards.noteEn: The dictionary form is the unchanged form ending in -ar, -er, or -ir. The ending identifies the person: sentir plus -á gives sentirá, and ver plus -á gives verá. A few common verbs change their stem, but use the same endings.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; begins de sobra
cards.noteEn: De combines with sobra to form de sobra, which says there is more than enough.

example.en: We have more than enough food.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that there is more than enough of something?
cards.answerEn: Use de sobra after the thing or amount that is plentiful.
cards.noteEn: The two words form a fixed expression for an ample surplus. It can follow nouns such as tiempo or dinero, or a verb such as haber or tener.

example.en: We have more than enough space.

cards.answerEn: more than enough; surplus (in de sobra)
cards.noteEn: Sobra normally relates to something left over. In de sobra, it completes a fixed expression for an ample surplus.

cards.questionEn: How do you refer to a set of equipment that reproduces audio?
cards.noteEn: De links sistema to sonido to name the system's function. The expression can cover speakers, an amplifier, and related audio equipment.

example.es: Instalaron un sistema de sonido nuevo.
example.en: They installed a new sound system.

cards.noteEn: Sonido can mean sound in general or a particular noise that can be heard.
Broma is a humorous remark, trick, or prank; context distinguishes a spoken joke from an action played on someone.
Esto is a neutral demonstrative for an unidentified thing, fact, or whole situation. It is not used directly before a noun.
Cuántos carries a written accent in a direct or indirect question and changes to cuántas before a feminine plural noun.
An audiófilo is a person strongly interested in high-quality sound reproduction and audio equipment. This masculine or mixed-group plural keeps the written accent.

cards.answerEn: are (as part of hacen falta, are needed)
cards.noteEn: In hacer falta, hacer changes to agree with what is needed. Hacen is used when the needed people or things are plural.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that someone or something is needed?
cards.answerEn: Use a form of hacer followed by falta; hacer agrees with what is needed.
cards.noteEn: For one needed thing, use hace falta. For several, use hacen falta. The needed item acts like the grammatical subject, so the form of hacer changes even though falta stays singular.

example.es: Hace falta una llave, pero hacen falta dos tornillos.
example.en: One key is needed, but two screws are needed.

cards.answerEn: needed; necessary (as part of hacer falta)
cards.noteEn: Falta combines with a form of hacer to say that someone or something is needed. It stays singular in this expression even when hacen is plural.

cards.answerEn: Use para followed by the verb’s dictionary form.
cards.noteEn: The dictionary form ends in -ar, -er, or -ir and is called the infinitive. Use para + verb when the same person or thing performs both actions: in estudio para aprender, I both study and learn. When someone else performs the second action, Spanish needs the different pattern para que.
cards.questionEn: How do you say “in order to do something” in Spanish?

example.en: I study in order to learn.

cards.noteEn: Cambiar can mean altering something or replacing one item with another; the surrounding object supplies the exact sense.

example.en: I am going to replace the battery.

cards.noteEn: Bombilla is the common word in Spain for the replaceable electric bulb in a lamp.
Te can mean “to you” when you are the recipient or the person affected by an action. It normally appears before a conjugated verb.
Lo replaces a masculine singular thing, or sometimes a whole idea, as the direct object. It normally appears before a conjugated verb.

example.es: Tengo el libro y lo leo.
example.en: I have the book and I’m reading it.

cards.answerEn: you could; you would be able to
cards.noteEn: Podrías is the conditional, or “would,” form of poder for one familiar person. Poder changes to the irregular stem podr- and adds -ías; the following action stays in its unchanged dictionary form.

cards.questionEn: How do you form a Spanish “would” verb such as “would forget”?
cards.answerEn: Keep the whole dictionary form and add a conditional ending such as -ía.
cards.noteEn: The same endings attach to verbs ending in -ar, -er, and -ir. The ending changes for the person: -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, or -ían.

cards.promptEs: poder + verbo en forma de diccionario
cards.questionEn: How do you say that someone can, could, or may do something?
cards.answerEn: Use a form of poder for the person and situation, then keep the action verb in its unchanged dictionary form.
cards.noteEn: Poder changes to forms such as puedo, puedes, puede, podemos, and pueden for present ability or possibility. Podría can present a possible or imagined option. The following action keeps its -ar, -er, or -ir ending.
Apreciar can mean valuing someone or recognizing and enjoying a quality in something.
Remate can be the final touch that completes something. In a joke, it is the line that delivers the payoff.

example.es: El remate del chiste sorprendió a todos.

cards.noteEn: Spanish writes de followed by the masculine singular word el as the single word del.

example.es: El color del coche es rojo.
example.en: The color of the car is red.

cards.noteEn: Chiste is a joke told for humor, often with a setup and a final punchline.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word here; part of a través de (“through”)

cards.questionEn: How do you say that something goes or can be seen through something?
cards.answerEn: Use a través de before the thing: it means “through” or “across.”
cards.noteEn: Keep all three parts together. Before masculine singular el, de and el combine as del: a través del bosque. Before a feminine noun, use a través de la, as in a través de la ventana. The expression can describe literal passage or a figurative means.

example.es: La luz entra a través de la ventana.
example.en: The light comes in through the window.

cards.answerEn: part of a través de, “through” or “across”
no separate English word; completes a través de, “through”

cards.noteEn: A códec is software or a method that encodes and decodes digital audio or video, often compressing it to use less data.

example.es: Este códec reduce el tamaño del audio.
example.en: This codec reduces the audio size.
